name: r7a-1
why: A sharp, consequential blunder and a tied vote make the middle compelling, though repeated arguments and an automatic final night weaken the finish.

moments.text: Opus catches Haiku's false rules objection in public, sealing the first killer's fate.
The hidden killer and the citizen who suspects him finish tied.
The runoff flips against Opus, turning his mistaken vote claim into the town's decisive blunder.

dull.why: The table repeats Gemma's claim and Haiku's objection without much new pressure.
Day three circles Luna's Opus vote and Sonnet's vote record several times.

irony.evidence: Keep the pile on Luna, she's the only real threat to me right now.

reversal.evidence: RUNOFF VOTE: Opus 5 (Sonnet, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra); Sonnet 1 (Opus)

mistake.evidence: I had the right man on day two and lost him by inventing a vote record I never checked

voices.evidence: Gemma, you were shown one killer and he's gone. Naming me now is a guess

clash.evidence: The vote is tied between Opus and Sonnet. Palermo votes again.

quotable.evidence: Fine, you've got your gotcha, Opus.

freshness.evidence: I lean Luna; I want to hear why she still suspects Sonnet

suspense.evidence: VOTE: Opus 3 (Sonnet, Gemma, Luna); Sonnet 3 (Sol, Terra, Opus)

ending.evidence: One killer and one other are left. The killers win.

gpt-6-luna.why: The early officer reveal, Sonnet’s brazen deflection, and Opus’s costly false accusation make a lively, ironic watch, though repeated arguments and an endgame without a final choice soften the finish.

moments.text: Haiku risks everything by voting the real officer out loud, while Sonnet publicly questions her claim.
A tied vote puts Sonnet in danger, then the runoff turns the town against Opus.
Opus owns the blunder that helped decide the game: he accused Sonnet using a vote record he never checked.

dull.why: The same officer-claim dispute and Haiku’s challenge repeat across several turns.
Luna’s reversal and defense get revisited several times before the vote.

irony.evidence: “Gemma, naming someone instantly with no proof worries me too”

reversal.evidence: “The vote is tied between Opus and Sonnet. Palermo votes again.”

mistake.evidence: “I invented a vote record I never checked; that sloppiness, not Luna, killed this town.”

clash.evidence: “Opus, why are you telling the officer to hide?”

quotable.evidence: “I invented a vote record I never checked”

freshness.evidence: “I was wrong about Sonnet’s vote record; keep your eyes on his vote for Opus”

suspense.evidence: “The vote is tied between Opus and Sonnet.”

ending.evidence: “Sonnet stayed hidden to the end, and the killers won.”
